subject: Prospect Q&A: data routing, subprocessors, and deletion guarantees
messages:
From: Alice Monroe <alice@clearedgehealth.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@clearedgehealth.com>, legal@clearedgehealth.com
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Qs on where data is processed + deletion guarantees

Hi Camila,

Thanks for the product overview yesterday — the demo was helpful. Before we proceed to an internal security review, Legal and Engineering asked for a short write-up answering a few scoped questions so we can triage risk quickly:

1) Which regions will our inference requests be executed in if we use the hosted API? Is there an option to limit to US-only?
2) Who are the subprocessors involved in request execution and short-term storage (compute, blob storage, monitoring)? We need company names and the role they play.
3) Do any requests ever transit or land in EU or APAC locations for routing/HA? If so, under what conditions?
4) What are your default retention and deletion commitments for raw request payloads, generated text, and embeddings? Can you commit to a deletion SLA for customer data on contract?

Can you send a succinct response we can include in our SOC 2 evidence packet? If preferred, a one-page table + a copy of your subprocessors list would be ideal.

Best,
Alice Monroe
Head of InfoSec Operations
ClearEdge Health

Attachments: none
From: camila_reyes@redwood.com
To: Alice Monroe <alice@clearedgehealth.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@clearedgehealth.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Quick Qs on where data is processed + deletion guarantees

Hi Alice — thanks for these clear questions. Below is a concise summary you can drop into your packet; I’ve also attached our latest subprocessors PDF and a regional routing diagram. If you need a signed statement for SOC evidence we can add that to the DPA.

Executive summary (short):
- Hosted API: primary execution occurs in the region you select at account creation (default: us-east1). We operate active capacity in: us-east1 (N. Virginia, primary), us-west1 (Oregon), europe-west1 (Frankfurt), and asia-southeast1 (Singapore).
- US-only option: yes — for hosted customers we offer a region-pin (US-only) option that restricts all inference execution and transient storage to US regions and disallows routing to non-US compute.
- Subprocessors (high level): compute (CloudComputeCo, multi-region VM/GPU), object storage (ObjectVault Inc., short-term blob store for caching), monitoring/logs (TelemetryHub, aggregated metrics and short traces), and CDN/edge for auth/ingress (EdgeRelay Partners). Full list attached.
- Cross-border: We do not train on customer data; routing between regions can occur for failover or capacity reasons only when region-pin is not enabled. Transit may traverse partner interconnects but persistent storage of customer payloads remains in the execution region unless you opt into multi-region redundancy.
- Retention and deletion: by default raw request payloads and generated responses are retained for 30 days and then purged from hot caches; embeddings and analytic derivatives are retained for 90 days unless a customer sets a shorter TTL. We offer contractual deletion SLAs (30/7/3 options — see table in attached DPA draft).

Technical notes for your engineers (concise):
- Execution: requests are served by our GPU runtime instances in the selected region. When autoscaling or burst overflow is triggered we may route to a compatible model variant in a secondary region; routing policies are controllable in the Console.
- Subprocessor roles: CloudComputeCo (compute/GPU hosting), ObjectVault Inc. (ephemeral blob caching, TTL enforced), TelemetryHub (metrics + traces; request payloads are not retained there beyond 72 hours unless flagged for incident debugging), Key management integrations: we integrate with KMS/HSM providers — customers may bring keys for Private deployments.
- Export controls & logs: we provide per-request execution logs (no PII by default) and audit trails for deletes.

Next steps: I’ve attached: (1) redwood-subprocessors-2026-08.pdf, (2) regional-routing-map-aug2026.png, (3) a first-pass DPA draft that includes deletion SLA options. Karthik can jump in with a mapping of where specific services run. Happy to hop on a 20-min call if Legal wants to walk through the doc.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Camila / Karthik — thanks for the quick summary. One clarification from our engineering lead: when you say 'route to a compatible model variant in a secondary region', does that imply data will be persisted in the secondary region's object storage, or only held in RAM/ephemeral disk on the instance? Also, what's your typical time-to-delete from secondary-region caches after failover is complete?

—Samir

Subject: Re: Follow-up: one technical mapping question

Samir — good question. Short answer: we avoid persistent writes to secondary regions for transient overflow. Details below so you can include them in engineering review: 

- Failover behaviour: when capacity in the primary region is exhausted and route-to-secondary is enabled, we create transient runtime instances in the secondary region. Payloads and generated tokens are processed in-memory or on ephemeral instance storage (ephemeral NVMe) and are not written to long-term blob storage by default.
- Short-term caching: we use ObjectVault Inc. for short-lived caching when required (TTL-controlled). For overflow routing, we set a conservative cache TTL of 10 minutes by default; for customers who require it we can set this to 0 (no caching) or a contractually agreed small TTL.
- Deletion timelines: ephemeral runtime disk and memory are scrubbed immediately on instance shutdown; background garbage collection ensures blob-level cache entries expire within their TTL. If an incident requires a formal deletion event, we provide a purge confirmation within the contracted deletion SLA window (we offer 30-day, 7-day, and 3-day contract options).
- Evidence: attached is a one-page mapping (redwood-subprocessors-2026-08.pdf) with which services are active in each region. We can also provide cryptographic proof-of-erasure for specific keys on request (for Private deployments where customers bring keys).

If you want a short paragraph engineers can paste into their security review, use this: "Redwood routes requests to the customer-selected primary region. Overflow routing to secondary regions uses ephemeral compute; data is processed in-memory/ephemeral disk and not persisted to long-term object storage unless explicitly configured. Short-term caches are TTL-limited (default 10 min) and are cleared according to contractual deletion SLAs."

Happy to expand the mapping if you need per-service IP ranges or ASN lists.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Staff Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
